title: Certificate-transparency log segment (v1)
description: One segment of the flat append-only certificate-transparency log: ct/{n}.json. The shape is FS-08 §12.1 (FS08-111) verbatim; at v0 the log is exactly one committed file, ct/0.json, appended by PR (FS08-113, VS-28). Entries carry hash, type, kind, ref and timestamp and NO PERSONAL DATA (CERT-031) — that is what makes the log GDPR-compatible and therefore immutable forever. scripts/ct-verify.mjs enforces append-only, monotonicity, well-formedness, the segment chain, and the no-personal-data rule.

segment.description: Segment number. v0 has only segment 0; rotation begins at P-M3 with segment 0 carried forward unchanged (FS08-113).

startSeq.description: Global sequence number of this segment's first entry. Must equal segment * entriesPerSegment (config/publish.json).

prevSegmentSha256.description: SHA-256 of the previous segment file's bytes; null for segment 0. This is what makes retroactive tampering provable across segment boundaries (FS08-135).

seq.description: Global monotonic sequence number, contiguous and strictly increasing from the segment's startSeq.

h.description: SHA-256 of the compact JWS string (CERT-030) — the hash of the SIGNED OBJECT, not of any rendered PDF. That is why a certificate's PDF need not be byte-deterministic at v0 (CERT-081) and why a signature that never landed in the log is harmless: verification requires log presence.

typ.description: JWS family. The first five values are the FS-00 §6.4 frozen certificate types; only `supporter` (payment certificate) and `license-status` (status certificate) are issuable at v0 (VS-30). `entitlement-record` and `ct-checkpoint` are the two NON-certificate JWS families that the v0 operator script also CT-appends (VS-27, FS08-113) — they are recorded here so a real v0 log validates. [HUMAN DECISION] If {ORG}/spec freezes different tokens for those two families, this enum is the single place to change.

kind.description: `issue` for a new object; `revoke` and `status` for later events, which are NEW ENTRIES referencing the original hash — the log never edits (CERT-033).

ref.description: For `revoke`/`status`, the `h` of the original entry; null for `issue`. ct-verify.mjs additionally requires the referenced hash to exist at a LOWER seq.

ts.description: UTC ISO-8601 instant, `Z` offset, second precision. Non-decreasing across the log.
